Faster insights. Fewer failures. DataMind Visual AI™ is an AI-enabled monitoring system that uses industrial cameras integrated with cutting-edge AI to deliver real-time visibility into critical failures and process inefficiencies across conveyors, crushers, feeders, and flotation cells. The system alerts weeks before deterioration develops into a failure and, if selected, can automatically stop the conveyor in unpredictable events to minimise damage. It is fully integrated with the DataMind AI™ platform, which monitors the rest of the equipment using oil, vibration, motor current, and pressure data – ensuring complete, holistic coverage of all potential failure modes across the site. Deterioration Monitoring & Trending AI-powered monitoring of a wide range of deteriorations and process inefficiencies that cannot be detected by other sensors. Oversize Ore Detects oversize boulders in real time – before they jam crushers or block chutes. Belt Misalignment Identifies gradual lateral drift to prevent edge wear or belt run-off. Belt Clip & Splice Automatically detects and monitors belt clip and splice conditions to save manual inspections and prevent belt rips. Optional Immediate Conveyor Stops Certain unpredictable events – such as a single oversized rock or a sudden belt rip caused by contamination – can’t be foreseen, yet require an instant response to avoid major damage. Stopping the conveyor immediately can significantly reduce repair time, cost, and belt damage. DataMind Visual AI™ integrates with SCADA, allowing operation teams to configure automatic belt stops in such high-risk scenarios, ensuring faster action and better protection for critical assets. Reduced lubrication quality accelerates gear and bearing wear, leading to costly rebuilds and extended downtime. DataMind AI continuously monitors transmission oil condition through oil analysis correlation and temperature trends, enabling early identification of contamination before damage progresses. In this case, DataMind AI flagged an oil analysis result from a GHH LHD Loader showing elevated contamination markers in the transmission fluid. Cross-referencing with transmission oil temperature telemetry, DataMind AI identified a subtle but consistent temperature elevation that had gone unnoticed in routine monitoring, a pattern consistent with the reduced lubrication efficiency caused by contaminated oil. By combining the oil analysis findings with the transmission temperature trend, DataMind AI identified active contamination as the root cause, most likely water ingress or coolant cross-contamination through a degraded oil cooler seal. The temperature signature confirmed that the oil’s viscosity and lubrication properties were already compromised, increasing gear and bearing wear rates. The maintenance team performed a transmission oil change and flush, then inspected the transmission oil cooler, finding a degraded internal seal allowing coolant ingress. Repairing the cooler and refreshing the oil prevented progressive gearbox damage. Early intervention avoided an estimated $42,000 in component replacement costs and saved 2 days of unplanned downtime.
